audits.title: SipTilSend: Sustainability of a Quality Improvement Initiative to Reduce Pre-operative Fluid Fasting in Orthopaedic Patients – A Re-audit PDSA Cycle

audits.title: A Quality Improvement Project to Assess if Preoperative Trauma Patients Are Receiving Their Prescribed Medications Preoperatively.

audits.setting: Trauma theatre list patients on orthopaedic/surgical wards, Basildon University Hospital

cycle1.result: 16/41 (39%) received their medications correctly; 22 critical drug class omissions; 19 omitted because nil by mouth.

audits.standard: Royal College of Nursing guidelines: minimum fasting of six hours for food and two hours for clear fluids before elective anaesthesia or sedation
audits.setting: Moorfields South Pre-operative Assessment Unit, St George's Hospital

cycle1.result: Policy stated nothing to eat or drink from midnight/7AM; patients not encouraged to drink clear fluids up to two hours before surgery; 70% subjective dehydration, 40% clinical evidence of dehydration; longest fast 17 hours.

cycle2.result: All patients encouraged to drink clear fluids until two hours before surgery; 25% subjective dehydration, 25% clinical evidence of dehydration; longest fast eight hours.

audits.other_findings: Patients in cycle 1 reported the instructions were clear despite being non-compliant with guidance.

audits.title: Adherence to Preoperative Fasting Guidelines in Elective Surgical Patients.
audits.standard: International (ASA/European Society of Anaesthesiology) and Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh fasting guidance: clear fluids until 2 hours and solids until 6 hours before surgery (morning list: solids to midnight, clear fluids to 06:30; afternoon list: breakfast before 07:00, clear fluids to 11:00)
audits.setting: Cardiac, thoracic and vascular surgery departments, RUDN University-affiliated teaching hospital, Moscow

cycle1.period: September (baseline audit; year given as 2022 in methods and 2023 in abstract)
cycle1.result: 86 (95.6%) fasted >2 hours from clear fluids and 90 (100%) >6 hours from solid food; 18 (20.0%) fasted >12 hours from clear fluids; 48 (53.3%) received both verbal and written instructions.

audits.intervention: Institutional action plan: explicit morning and afternoon fasting rules, fasting information at pre-hospitalisation and preoperative clinic visits, and explanatory leaflets for patients.

cycle2.period: December (final monthly re-audit after October and November)
cycle2.result: 33 of 57 (57.9%) fasted >2 hours from clear fluids (p=0.021); 27 (47.4%) fasted >6-12 hours from solid food (p=0.005); 3 (5.3%) fasted >12 hours from clear fluids.

audits.other_findings: Across all 306 patients median fasting was 4.5 hours for clear fluids and 14.5 hours for solids; afternoon-list patients fasted longer (clear fluids 6.2 vs 3.4 hours, p<0.001). Both instruction types were received by 70.3% after the action plan.
audits.citation: Sidik AI, Lishchuk A, Faybushevich AN, Moomin A, Akambase J, Dontsov V, et al.. Adherence to Preoperative Fasting Guidelines in Elective Surgical Patients. Cureus. 2024;16(10):e71554. doi:10.7759/cureus.71554. PMID: 39544576.
